snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, Clostridium difficile (C. diff) is a reportable disease in many jurisdictions worldwide

text_blocks.snippet: In the United States, C. diff is a healthcare-associated infection (HAI) that must be reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) through the National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN). Additionally, some states may require healthcare providers or laboratories to report C. diff cases to their local health departments.
Other countries may also have reporting requirements for C. diff. For example, in Canada, C. diff is a reportable disease in Ontario, Manitoba, and Alberta.
Reporting C. diff helps public health officials track the incidence of the infection, identify outbreaks, and implement measures to prevent its spread.
